title: Fitness influencers are giving you body dysmorphia?! (Response to Geoffrey Verity Schofield)
summary: A supportive response to Geoffrey Verity Schofield's video on body dysmorphia. NH argues BDD is contagious and not born in a vacuum: enhanced influencers inflate physique standards, widening the gap with their natural audience and driving either despair or steroid use, while selling solutions to the problem they created. His remedies: choose realistic natural role models, stop scheming and just train, unfollow enhanced influencers, and reject the standards.
claims: Body/muscle dysmorphia is not born in a vacuum; it arises from comparison with others and is passed person to person like a contagious disease in the fitness community
The BDD cycle: someone feels small, takes drugs, then makes everyone around them feel smaller, inflating physique standards locally and on social media
BDD has two outcomes: depression that robs the joy of lifting and leads to quitting, or steroid use leading to organ damage and early death
Steroids don't cure body dysmorphia; they make everything bigger, including the dysmorphia
Body dysmorphia levels have skyrocketed compared to 30 years ago because of the modern media environment
The greater the distance between you and your physique role model, the worse the dysmorphia; enhanced influencers keep growing while their natural audience does not
Drug users give bad advice and cannot help naturals grow
Natural golden-era bodybuilders like Jack LaLanne in the 1940s were impressive yet realistic, so choose them as role models to reduce dysmorphia
Modern mass monsters no longer look human; shown to people a century ago they'd be seen as demigods or Frankenstein creatures
Physique inflation is everywhere: film, toys, bodybuilding; even action figures have grown
A physique is a healthy male power fantasy if you take motivation from it knowing you won't look like it; it becomes BDD fuel once you're deluded into thinking it's naturally achievable
Widespread steroid awareness plants doubt about every big physique, disconnecting you from it so it brings despair instead of inspiration
Genetics talk became prevalent alongside steroids; enhanced lifters invoke genetics to justify physiques built on drugs, which are 'injectable genetics'
Distorted standards split people into the deluded who think they'll look like an IFBB pro on rice and broccoli and the blackpilled who think no muscle is possible, with movement between the two
BDD paralyses you into scheming instead of training, or drives you to overtrain and injure yourself
Stop thinking about inflated standards and just train; 1940s lifters didn't debate whether they'd get 19-inch arms, they did the work
Influencers create the body dysmorphia and then sell you programs and products to fix it
NH still has days where he looks in the mirror and feels tiny; it never fully goes away
Destigmatize the person, not the illness; normalizing BDD itself removes the drive to fix it, and the pain is the signal the problem remains
Enhanced influencers are also victims of BDD; many who died recently chose death over losing size
Unfollow enhanced influencers, for your sake and theirs, since audience pressure keeps them on drugs
Greg Doucette's extreme standards, which apply only to genetic elites or drug users, project dysmorphia and blackpill his audience toward drug use
NH had severe BDD a few years ago and made big progress using the practices from his own videos
You need no standards, only your own body, mind, knowledge and constant progression
